**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve filters for context-bound CiFn resources**

Do not expose `cifn.jobs.list` as an ordinary generic collection page without supplying its required `filter.runId`. After the dedicated CiFn routes were removed, opening the generated Jobs card requests this operation with no filter and fails schema validation; Logs and Artifacts have the same problem, requiring `runId` or `runId` plus `jobKey`. This also removes the previous run-detail navigation that supplied those values, leaving operators unable to browse jobs, logs, or artifacts through the console.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Group presentation operations by their declared target**

Resolve presentation operations from `operation.target.resource`, not from the middle segment of the operation ID. A valid manifest can declare `examplefn.enumerate` targeting `records` and set it as `records.presentation.listOperationId`; the validator accepts that explicit binding, but the `operations` array here was grouped under `enumerate`, so the declared `records` metadata is never found and the generic UI exposes the wrong resource without its presentation. This breaks the manifest-driven extension contract for operation IDs that do not follow the inferred `{module}.{resource}.{verb}` convention.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Document the provider-selected CSRF header**

Do not hard-code `X-Operator-CSRF` for the generic invocation endpoint when authentication now supplies `principal.authentication.csrfHeaderName`. The shipped AuthFn bridge projects `x-authfn-csrf`, and another provider may choose a different name, so clients generated from this OpenAPI operation will send a header that `authorizeMutation` does not recognize and cookie-authenticated mutations will be rejected. The OpenAPI configuration needs the provider's actual header name or must avoid claiming this fixed name.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply default sorting before pagination**

Avoid implementing `defaultSort` by sorting only the already-paginated response. For any cursor-backed resource whose provider order differs from the presentation order, each page is sorted independently, so an item on the next page can belong before items shown on the current page and traversal is not globally ordered as advertised. Pass the requested sort to a supporting list operation or leave provider ordering intact unless the full collection is available.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

SFN-22 Make Super Console function-agnostic and manifest-driven

## Executive summary Refactor Super Console so its core discovers modules, relationships, navigation, resources, operations, and optional surfaces from supplied administration manifests and adapters instead of hard-coded Superfunction identifiers. The goal is for dev-only, next-only, and third-party functions to integrate without modifying Super Console core. ## Problem or opportunity The current implementation is adapter-driven at dispatch time, but Super Console still contains a fixed 29-module catalog and concrete knowledge of functions such as RecFn, SecFn, CiFn, SearchFn, WatchFn, CatchFn, ContentFn, and LogFn. It also contains function-specific routes, UI behavior, service wording, authentication integration, and tests. This creates branch-coupling between `sf-next/next` and dev: porting the console to dev would also carry metadata and specialized behavior for functions that do not exist there. Adding a new function can also require modifying the console itself. ## Expected outcome A function-agnostic Super Console core that can render and operate an arbitrary valid admin capability adapter without source changes. Function-specific authentication, automation transports, and rich UI experiences are supplied as optional integrations owned outside the core. ## Goals * Derive the module catalog from supplied `AdminCapabilityAdapter.manifest` values. * Use manifest `availability`, `owner`, and `dependencies` fields for nesting, folding, and validation. * Keep generic module, resource-list, resource-detail, and action routes as the default UI. * Extend generic presentation metadata where existing rich workflows cannot be represented truthfully. * Move specialized function UI and route behavior behind optional, function-owned extensions. * Remove SearchFn/WatchFn checks from generic surface enablement; rely on injected services and authorized surface projection. * Separate the AuthFn convenience adapter from the generic console runtime. * Evaluate splitting McpFn projection/transport into an optional bridge so the shared admin kernel and console core do not require a concrete automation provider. * Preserve fail-closed authorization, scope, confirmation, audit, redaction, idempotency, REST/OpenAPI, client, and disabled-module behavior. ## Non-goals * Removing UIFn as the console's visual implementation. * Reimplementing function domain logic in the console. * Automatically synchronizing the resulting changes to `origin/dev`. * Changing existing non-admin function SDK contracts. * Implementing or opening a pull request as part of this backlog capture. ## Acceptance criteria * Super Console core contains no fixed catalog or display-name map for concrete product functions. * A synthetic adapter such as `examplefn` or `custom-product` receives navigation, generic resource pages, actions, REST/OpenAPI, and permitted automation exposure without changing console source. * Owner, folded, nested, unavailable, and dependency behavior is driven entirely by validated manifests. * Generic navigation and search availability contain no checks for named function IDs. * Function-specific routes and presentation code are either represented generically through manifest metadata or moved to explicit optional extensions. * Core authentication accepts the generic operator-auth contract; the AuthFn implementation is function-owned and structurally compatible. * Disabled or absent functions expose no navigation, route, OpenAPI operation, client operation, or tool. * Existing safety, tenancy, authorization, confirmation, audit, redaction, and idempotency tests remain green. * Regression tests prove arbitrary module IDs work and prevent new concrete function IDs from entering core. * Migration and rollback guidance explains how current Super Console installations retain behavior. ## Dependencies and risks * Extending the manifest schema may require coordinated updates to `@superfunctions/admin`, all affected admin packages, generated clients, validation, and documentation. * Removing specialized CiFn pages can reduce operator usability unless presentation metadata or an extension API covers those workflows first. * Moving AuthFn or McpFn integrations can introduce package graph or publication-order changes. * SvelteKit route/component extension loading must remain buildable, type-safe, and safe for self-hosted deployments. * The future dev sync should occur only after this refactor is stable on `sf-next/next`. ## Open questions * **Open question:** Should rich UI extensions be compile-time Svelte modules, framework-neutral presentation descriptors, or both? * **Open question:** Should McpFn integration remain an optional feature of Super Console or move to a separate `@superfunctions/admin-mcp` package? * **Open question:** Which existing CiFn-specific workflows require a rich extension after generic presentation metadata is expanded? * **Open question:** Should AuthFn's console adapter live in `@authfn/admin` or a dedicated `@authfn/superconsole` package? * **Assumption:** [SFN-21](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFN-21/build-super-console-as-the-modular-self-hosted-administration-control) remains the completed parent delivery and this work is a compatible architectural follow-up. ## Supporting documents * [Ideation & Product Rationale — SFN-22: Make Super Console function-agnostic and manifest-driven]() * [Architecture & Delivery Plan — SFN-22: Make Super Console function-agnostic and manifest-driven]()
